     SOUTHERN MENARD COUNTY LANDOWNER GROUP'S INITIAL BRIEF


       COMES NOW, Southern Menard County Landowner Group, hereinafter referred to as

(" Southern Menard County Landowner Group") and file this Brief following the Hearing on the

Merits and would show the ALJ's as follows:

                                        INTRODUCTION

         Southern Menard County Landowner Group has a justiciable interest in this Project

  because Links M8, P42, P41 or M42, fragment and would run through property owned by

  Southern Menard County Landowner Group. All members of Southern Menard County

  Landowner Group were admitted as intervenors to this docket.


                                        SUMMARY OF POSITION

         The primary issue in this proceeding is which route best satisfies the criteria set forth in

  the Public Utility Regulatory Act ("PURA") and the Substantive Rules of the Public Utility

  Commission ("PUC' or "Commission"). The record shows that Route 894, or at a minimum any

  route that avoids Link M8, P42, P41 or M42, better satisfies the criteria because Route 894 and all
  routes that avoid Link M8, P42, P41 or M42 more reasonably moderate impacts on landowners,

 community values, and environmental resources while maintaining reasonable costs to

 consumers. We are opposed to routes 266,304, 376, 739,911, 913, and 914 ("Opposed

 Routes").

         Through the testimony of multiple parties, the record establishes that lower-impact

 alternatives to any route that utilizes Link M8, P42, P41 or M42 exist and better satisfy PURA

 and the Commission's routing criteria. Among those alternatives, Route 894 is the best-

 supported option in the record and was identified by the Applicants as the route that best meets

 the requirements of PURA and the Commission's Substantive Rules.

       Accordingly, the Commission should select Route 894 or, at a minimum, reject any route

that utilizes Link M8, P42, P41 or M42.

                            Ill.    PRELIMINARY ORDER ISSUES

         This Initial Brief will not address the following issues from the Preliminary Order:

 Application, Notice, Public Input, Need, Best Management Practices, Texas Parks and Wildlife

 Department, Permits, Coastal Management Program, or Limitation of Authority. This Initial Brief

 will address the Route and Cost to Consumers.

         a.      Route

         PURA § 37.056(c)(4) requires the Commission to consider several factors when

 determining whether to grant a certificate for a transmission line, including community values,

 recreational and park areas, historical and aesthetic values, and environmental integrity. The

 Commission's Substantive Rules also require that transmission lines should reasonably

 moderate impacts on affected communities and landowners while considering costs.

 Factors to consider when determining impacts on communities and landowners include whether

 the routes parallel property lines or other natural or cultural features and whether the routes
   conform with the policy of prudent avoidance, which focuses on minimizing exposure to

  electric and magnetic fields.

        Links P42, M8, M42 and P41 fragment many of Southern Menard County Landowner Group's

  property and does not support the positive values identified by PURA or the Substantive Rule of the

  Commission, as these Links does not parallel existing property lines, roads, and/or existing utility

  lines. Additionally, the use of the above mentioned Links will affect the aesthetic value of the

  properties, and cause impacts on habitable structures are ranching operations. Utilizing Link

  P42, M8, M42, or P41 for the transmission line route will significantly impede the operation

  of several ranches as working ranches, recreational ranches, and hunting businesses. When

  compared to the Opposed Routes, Route 894 holistically moderates impacts on

  communities and landowners. Route 894 is a lower-impact routing alternative when compared to

  the Opposed Routes because the Opposed Routes impact more habitable structures. Route 894

  performs strongly on prudent avoidance, with 85 habitable structures within 500 feet of its

  centerline.1 Route 487 only identified 96 habitable structures within 500 feet of its centerline.2

  Therefore, Southern Menard County Landowner Group agrees with the Applicants and PUC

  Staff that Route 894 or Route 487 best meets the requirements of the PURA and Commission

  Substantive Rules for the Project. The cost to consumers reinforces Southern Menard

  County Landowner Group' s conclusion that Route 894 should be selected by the Commission.


           b. Cost to Consumers

           Route 894 is among the least expensive routes, and is one of the shortest routes at 223.2

  Miles.3 Route 894 is the Applicants' identified best-meets route and performs favorably on cost,

  with an estimated transmission line cost of $1,680,919,000 and a total estimated proj ect cost of

   $2,076,387,000.4 Specifically, the Opposed Routes inflict a higher impact that Route 894 because

 the Opposed Routes: (i) have a higher number of habitable structures within 500 feet of the

 proposed centerline ofthe right-of-way (Route 894 has only 85)5; and are longer.

           The Commission should give significant weight to the fact that either Route 894 or

  Route 487 achieves the Applicants' project objectives at a lower cost than any of Routes 266,

  304,376, 739, 911, 913, and 914,6 while simultaneously avoiding the severe impacts to the

  Southern Menard County Landowner Group.

           With Route 894 being one of the least expensive routes and considering the overall

  benefits, Route 894 is the route the Commission should select.

           c.       Other Routes We Support/Do Not Oppose

           We also do not oppose the selection of Route 894 Western Mod. 1, 392, or 487. None of

           these Routes contain Link M8, P42, P41 or M42, and moderate the impacts to the

           Community better than the opposed routes.

                                              IV.      CONCLUSION


           The Opposed Routes do not reasonably balance the criteria set forth in PURA and the

  Commission's Substantive Rules when compared with Route 894. The record supports

  selecting Route 894 because it better moderates impacts on landowners, community values, and

  environmental resources while remaining reasonably cost competitive. Southern Menard

  County Landowner Group therefore respectfully requests that the Administrative Law Judges

  recommend Route 894,487, or, at a minimum, reject any route that utilizes Links M8, P42,

  P41, or M32.
